questions.q: What does stg_jaffle_shop__customers.sql do to the `id` column from raw_customers?
options: Drops it entirely since it's not needed
Aggregates it to count total customers
Renames it to customer_id — the only real transformation in this file
Joins it against the raw_orders table
questions.explain: The staging model's only real change is renaming id to customer_id — first_name and last_name pass through unchanged, and no joins or aggregation happen here.

questions.q: Why should this staging model have the exact same row count as raw_customers?
options: Because the 1:1 rule means staging models preserve the source's grain — no joins or aggregation change the row count
Because Snowflake enforces identical row counts between a source and any model built on it
Row counts don't need to match; staging models are allowed to change the grain
Because dbt automatically deduplicates rows in every staging model
questions.explain: A staging model's defining rule is 1:1 with its source — same grain, same row count — which is exactly what distinguishes it from an intermediate or mart model.

questions.q: Where would business logic like 'what counts as an active customer' belong, according to this lesson?
options: In stg_jaffle_shop__customers.sql, right after the rename
In the mart model (Lesson 8), never in the staging model
In the raw_customers table itself, via an UPDATE statement
In the sources.yml file from Lesson 5
questions.explain: Staging models are strictly light cleanup — renaming and casting. Business logic like defining 'active customer' belongs downstream, in the mart layer.

questions.q: Why is renaming id to customer_id worth doing, even in a model this small?
options: id is ambiguous across a whole project, while customer_id is unambiguous everywhere it shows up downstream
It makes the query run faster
Snowflake does not allow a column to be named id
dbt requires every primary key column to be named with an _id suffix
questions.explain: Making the rename once, in staging, means every downstream model and test inherits the clear, unambiguous customer_id name for free.

questions.q: What command builds only this one staging model, instead of the whole project?
options: dbt run --select stg_jaffle_shop__customers
dbt debug --model stg_jaffle_shop__customers
dbt init stg_jaffle_shop__customers
dbt test stg_jaffle_shop__customers
questions.explain: dbt run --select <model> builds just the named model, which is useful for confirming one specific model works without rebuilding the whole project.
